headword: {悪性腫瘍|あくせいしゅよう}

definitions.explanation: A cancerous tumor that grows uncontrollably and can invade surrounding tissues or spread to other parts of the body. The medical term for cancer viewed as a physical mass.

examples.japanese: {悪性腫瘍|あくせいしゅよう}が{見|み}つかった。
{検査|けんさ}の{結果|けっか}、{悪性腫瘍|あくせいしゅよう}の{疑|うたが}いがあると{言|い}われた。
examples.english: The test results showed a suspected malignant tumor.

examples.japanese: {悪性腫瘍|あくせいしゅよう}を{早期|そうき}に{発見|はっけん}すれば、{治療|ちりょう}の{選択肢|せんたくし}が{広|ひろ}がる。
examples.english: If a malignant tumor is found at an early stage, the treatment options become broader.

notes:
Composed of {悪性|あくせい} (malignant, bad-natured) and {腫瘍|しゅよう} (tumor, swelling). In medical usage, tumors are classified as either {悪性|あくせい} (malignant) or {良性|りょうせい} (benign). An {悪性腫瘍|あくせいしゅよう} is essentially what is meant by {がん} (cancer) in everyday speech, but the medical term is more precise and appears in diagnoses, test results, and clinical discussions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {悪性腫瘍|あくせいしゅよう}が{見|み}つかる: a malignant tumor is found
- {悪性腫瘍|あくせいしゅよう}の{疑|うたが}い: suspicion of a malignant tumor
- {悪性腫瘍|あくせいしゅよう}を{摘出|てきしゅつ}する: to remove a malignant tumor (surgically)
- {悪性腫瘍|あくせいしゅよう}が{転移|てんい}する: the malignant tumor metastasizes

RELATED TERMS:
- {良性腫瘍|りょうせいしゅよう}: benign tumor
- {がん}: cancer (the everyday word)
- {癌|がん}: cancer (in kanji; often used for carcinomas specifically)
- {腫瘍|しゅよう}: tumor (general term)
- {転移|てんい}: metastasis
- {摘出|てきしゅつ}: surgical removal, excision
